You may write scratch files under /tmp. Do NOT write anything to /output or /workspace.
Run MANY cases (30+). Be systematic and adversarial: hunt for cases where a naive JS port would diverge.

YOUR DIMENSION: Optional-argument parsing structure. Cover: long-option abbreviation (--k, --ke, --v, --va, --h, --he) and any ambiguity errors; --opt=value syntax including --val= (empty) and --key=; repeated options (last wins?); option value that itself looks like an option (--key --val, --val --key); values starting with a single dash that are negative numbers (--key -5, --val -5, --key -5.5, --key -x); the '--' pseudo-argument in every position (leading, trailing, middle, doubled); extra positionals; unknown options (-k, --keyx, --nope) and whether the "required" error pre-empts the "unrecognized arguments" error; missing one/both required options; interaction of -h/--help with missing required options and with invalid values (does help win?); empty-string option name/value; duplicated '--key=x --key y'. Report the exact stderr text and exit code for each error class.

surprises: `--=x` is the ONE reachable ambiguity in this parser: it partitions to prefix '--', which prefix-matches --help/--key/--val (not -h). Message: `ambiguous option: --=x could match --help, --key, --val`.
The ambiguity check runs in the argv PRE-SCAN, before ANY action executes — so `-h --=x` exits 2 with the ambiguity error instead of printing help. Nothing beats it except a preceding `--`.

A TRAILING `--` is reported as an unrecognized argument (`unrecognized arguments: --`), and doubled trailing `--`s report BOTH (`-- --`). The `--`-stripping in argparse only applies to argument lists consumed by an action, never to extras. Almost every naive JS port strips all `--` and diverges here.

`--` immediately after `--key`/`--val` does NOT get skipped to find the real value — it errors `expected one argument` (for optionals argparse deletes all '-' from the nargs regex, so the pattern is '(A)').

`-hx`, `-hel`, `-help`, `-he`, `-h5`, `-hh` ALL print help and exit 0. The unknown leftover ('-x', '-e', '-5', ...) is dropped into extras and parsing stops, but the already-queued -h action still fires. Meanwhile `-h-` and `-h--` error with `ignored explicit argument`.
Only U+0020 SPACE makes a dash-leading token count as a positional. `--key $'\ta'` (tab) is still treated as an unknown option and silently discarded, producing a confusing `required: --key` error.
The required-arguments error ALWAYS pre-empts unrecognized-arguments (different call layers). You can never see both in one run.
Error messages name the CANONICAL option (`argument --key:`) even when the user typed an abbreviation like `--k`/`--ke`; for help it's the slash-joined `argument -h/--help:`.
Help wins or loses purely by POSITION: `--h --val=x` -> help/exit 0, `--val=x --h` -> int error/exit 2.
prog is `os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])` — invoking via a symlink named `zzz-name` produces `usage: zzz-name ...`. A name with a space (`My Prog`) is used verbatim.

Usage wrapping depends on COLUMNS (shutil.get_terminal_size, minus 2). At COLUMNS=40 the usage wraps to `usage: test6_executable [-h] --key KEY\n                        --val VAL`; at <=30 it breaks after the prog name with a 7-space continuation indent. Default (no tty, no COLUMNS) is 80, which fits on one line.

`--key=` gives the empty string (prints False), while `--val=` gives the empty string that then fails int() with `invalid int value: ''` — the same syntax produces two totally different error classes.

PASS 1 (pre-scan classifier) over argv, producing a pattern array of 'O' / 'A' / '-': iterate i=0..n-1; if argv[i] === '--' push '-' and then push 'A' for EVERY remaining token and break out of classification. Otherwise call parseOptional(argv[i]); null -> 'A', else -> 'O' and record the resolved tuple at index i. Any ambiguity error MUST be raised during this pass, before any action runs.

parseOptional(s) implementation, in this exact order: (1) if s === '' return null; (2) if s[0] !== '-' return null; (3) if optionTable has exact s, return {action, optionString: s, sep: null, explicitArg: null}; (4) if s.length === 1 return null (bare '-' is a value); (5) const eq = s.indexOf('='); if eq !== -1 and optionTable has s.slice(0,eq), return {action, optionString: s.slice(0,eq), sep: '=', explicitArg: s.slice(eq+1)}; (6) tuples = getOptionTuples(s); if tuples.length > 1 -> fatal `ambiguous option: ${s} could match ${tuples.map(t=>t.optionString).join(', ')}`; if length === 1 return it; (7) if /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/.test(s) return null (negative number, no negative-number-looking options exist); (8) if s.includes(' ') return null (SPACE ONLY — do not use \s); (9) return {action: null, optionString: s} meaning UNKNOWN OPTION (still pattern 'O').

Else (single dash, s[1] !== '-'): shortPrefix = s.slice(0,2), shortExplicit = s.slice(2); for each entry: if optionString === shortPrefix push {optionString, sep:'', explicitArg: shortExplicit}; else if optionString.startsWith(s) push {optionString, sep:'', explicitArg: null}.

PASS 2 (left-to-right consumption). Maintain namespace {key: undefined, val: undefined} and an `extras` array. Walk i from 0; if pattern[i] === 'O' handle the option (possibly consuming i+1), else push argv[i] to extras and i++. Stop classification effects at the '--' index: from there on everything is pattern 'A' so it all goes to extras (including the '--' token itself, which has pattern '-' and is likewise never consumed -> it MUST end up in extras).

consumeOptional logic for a resolved tuple: if action is null (unknown option) -> extras.push(token); i++. If explicitArg != null: for the help action (nargs 0), replicate the cluster loop — if sep is '=' OR explicitArg[0] === '-' -> fatal `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '${explicitArg}'`; otherwise queue the help action, then try optionString = '-' + explicitArg[0]; if that is a known option, recurse with explicitArg = explicitArg.slice(1) (empty -> sep/explicitArg = null); if unknown, extras.push('-' + explicitArg) and STOP consuming, but STILL run the queued help action. For --key/--val (nargs 1) the explicitArg is simply the value.

If explicitArg is null and the action takes one argument: the value slot must be pattern 'A' at i+1. Concretely: if i+1 >= argv.length OR pattern[i+1] !== 'A' -> fatal `argument ${canonicalName}: expected one argument`. canonicalName is '--key' or '--val' (NEVER the abbreviation the user typed); for help it is '-h/--help' (option strings joined with '/').

Type conversion is EAGER and per-occurrence: every time --val is assigned, run the int conversion immediately and on failure emit `argument --val: invalid int value: '<raw>'` and exit 2 — do not defer to end of parse. Repeated options are plain last-wins overwrites.

Python repr for the error strings: values are wrapped in single quotes. For the inputs in scope ('' , 'x', '-5.5', '--', '3.0') a plain `'` + s + `'` is correct; only add escaping if you care about values containing quotes/backslashes.

Extras are joined with a single ' ' and inserted raw (no quoting, no escaping) — an empty-string extra contributes nothing but still consumes a separator, so two empty extras render as `unrecognized arguments:   ` (colon + space + space).
